item.title: Needed 1+1, Built a Functional Programming Language
item.description: graphLang I was given a pretty straightforward data structures problem: convert an arithmetic expression into a binary tree. Naturally, instead of stopping there, I decided to build an evaluator for it. Then I had a thought. What if the evaluator didn’t actually need to know what the operations were? A few days later I was implementing closures, a garbage collector, and a custom memory allocator in C. I had started with 1 + 1.

item.title: My First Terminal Post
item.description: Why I chose this stack I wanted a blog that I could write from the comfort of my terminal. No Javascript, no heavy frameworks, just pure markdown and HTML. Features of this setup: Zero javascript (0 bytes) Perfect rendering in w3m and lynx Instantly deployed to Vercel via Git Fast enough to compile 10,000 posts in milliseconds Here’s an example of some code, which renders perfectly as text: git add .
